title: Introduce dep-rotation scheduler, lightweight release-smoke check, and unify lint entrypoints
author: Maya Chen
ci_status: pass (release-smoke rerun once due to transient infra timeout)
description:
Motivation: Our dependency-rotation process has relied on ad-hoc scripts and manual windows which causes noisy PRs and occasional infra churn during releases. This change introduces a lightweight scheduler + coordinator for rotating non-critical transitive deps, a pre-release smoke-check workflow that runs a small matrix of critical integration paths before tagging releases, and a small refactor that normalizes lint entrypoints across TS/Python/Go packages to reduce CI surface area.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds .github/actions/dep-rotation-scheduler.yml: a scheduled action that triggers a coordinator which selects eligible modules for rotation and opens atomic PRs with clear risk metadata. Rotations are rate limited and honor per-repo exclusion lists.
- Adds .github/workflows/release-smoke.yml: a lightweight workflow that runs on release candidates and validates 3 critical flows (API compile, hosted runtime smoke, basic e2e for console). It is intentionally small and fast (~6-8m).
- Introduces scripts/dep-rotate/scheduler.py: coordinator logic and dry-run mode used in PRs for visibility.
- Unifies lint entrypoints by moving from multiple bespoke scripts to tools/lint/entrypoint.ts and small wrappers in package.json; this removes duplicate environment bootstrapping across repos.
- Updates ci/README.md with operator guidance, rotation windows, and rollback steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Scheduler dry-run mode implemented and tested locally
- [x] Release smoke workflow validated in staging (reran once after transient timeout)
- [x] Lint entrypoint smoke-tested across python, ts, go packages
- [x] Added Linear tasks and documentation for SRE/operators

Risk & mitigation: Rotations could introduce dependency incompatibilities. The scheduler uses a staged rollout: always opens PRs as drafts and annotates risk (major bump vs patch), runs dependency-compatibility CI job before marking PR ready. Releases run the smoke-check before final tag. Operators can opt-out repos via .github/dep-rotation-ignore.yml.

Why not a monolithic bot: We intentionally split the scheduler (coordinator) from the PR runner so operators can inspect dry-run output and hand-off high risk rotations rather than having an automated merge. This keeps noise low while enabling automation for low-risk updates.
